## TL;DR

The handoff gate failed on one browser test: at 1280px the Agents sub-tab strip clipped its last tab, "Model routing". The strip hid its scrollbar and did not wrap on desktop widths, so the tab could not be reached. I changed the strip to wrap at every width, the same fix #1139 applied to phones, and updated the one stylesheet assertion that pinned the old behaviour. The QA file and the five related Agents and Settings test files pass (113 tests). The scoped `repoos check --changed main` is running; this draft will be checked against its result before handoff.

## Work and rationale

The queued failure was specific: `Agents → Model routing at 1280px: no overflow, named controls, visible focus`. Running that single test reproduced it exactly. The audit reported `selected tab is scrolled out of its strip: button#agents-tab-model-routing.tab-btn`. The other checks in that test (overflow, control names, focus change) passed for that page.

The cause was CSS in `src/ui-app/src/style.css`. `.agent-tabs` was a flex row with `flex-wrap: nowrap`, `overflow-x: auto`, and a hidden scrollbar. Only the 900px media query made it wrap. At 1280px the thirteen-odd tabs are wider than the strip, so the trailing tabs are clipped with no visible scrollbar to reveal them. A sighted user at desktop width could not reach "Model routing" or "Budget Controls" without already knowing they were there.

I considered two alternatives:

- **Scroll the selected tab into view on load.** This keeps one row, but the other clipped tabs stay undiscoverable, and the hidden scrollbar still hides the overflow. It fixes the audit's symptom and leaves the real problem in place.
- **Show the scrollbar.** This makes overflow visible but gives a scroll bar inside a tab row, which is a worse control than a wrapped row on a desktop.

I chose wrapping. `.agent-tabs` now has `flex-wrap: wrap` and no `overflow-x`, at every width. The 900px block still sets the touch-sized tab height and lets labels wrap. `ChecksView.vue` also uses the `agent-tabs` class, so its strip wraps too; no test covers that strip's width, and the change is the same as the one already in use on phones.

I also updated `src/ui-app/tests/mobile-touch-affordances.test.ts`. Its assertion pinned `flex-wrap: wrap; overflow-x: visible` inside the 900px block. It now checks the base rule for `flex-wrap: wrap` and asserts that no `overflow-x: auto` remains on `.agent-tabs`. That is a deliberate change of contract, recorded here so the reviewer does not read it as weakening a test.

Verification in this session: `bun run build:ui` (UI rebuilt before the browser tests, since they run against the built app). Then the five affected files under the UI Vitest config, which carries the Vue plugin: `settings-agents-budget-qa-browser`, `mobile-touch-affordances`, `agents-view-cards`, `budget-controls-panel`, `model-routing-panel`. All 113 tests passed.

I did not add new tests for the wrap. The existing headless QA file already covers every Agents and Settings tab at 375, 768 and 1280, and it caught this failure, so it is the regression guard for this class.

## Approaches tried

- First run of the failing test with the root Vitest config failed to load the three Vue-based suites ("invalid JS syntax … install @vitejs/plugin-vue"). The cause was the config, not the code: those suites must run with `--config src/ui-app/vite.config.ts`. Rerunning with that config gave a clean result.
- The scroll-into-view option above was rejected for the reasons given.

## Challenges and blockers

- The queued message named the failing test as "visible focus on bee". The actual failure was a clipped selected tab, not a focus problem. I went by the test output, not the message.
- The scoped `repoos check --changed main` runs the build, format and lint, and the UI smoke test; it takes longer than the tool timeout, so it was moved to the background. Its final result is not in this draft yet.
- Nothing needed a human: no device, account or runner is involved. The visual evidence is the declared shots, which RepoOS captures at handoff on the final tree. The earlier review noted the existing captures were one commit stale, so they are re-captured at handoff.

## Key learnings

- A hidden scrollbar on a horizontally scrolling tab row is a clipping bug, not a style choice. On any width where the tabs don't fit, the last tabs are unreachable. Wrapping is safer than scrolling for a short fixed set of destinations.
- A CSS fix can break a test that pins the old CSS. When a test asserts a stylesheet rule, update the assertion to the new contract and say so in the report, rather than re-adding dead rules to satisfy it.
- Run the failing test alone first. The queued message's wording ("focus on bee") would have sent the search to focus styling. The test output named the real cause in one line.
